Focus Financial Partners: Acquisition Of ML Management Partners Expands Entertainment Industry Business Management Services
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 8:53 AM
Focus Financial Partners: Acquisition Of ML Management Partners Expands Entertainment Industry Business Management Services
Focus Financial Partners, a financial services firm providing wealth management, family office, and business management services, has acquired ML Management Partners (MLM), a New York City-based business management firm specializing in serving entertainment industry professionals and high-net-worth individuals. The transaction closed on November 1, 2026, and strengthens Focus’s business management platform with additional expertise serving clients in television, film, and related creative industries.
Founded in 1988 by Mark Landesman, ML Management Partners provides business management and family office services to entertainment professionals, including actors, comedians, directors, producers, writers, industry executives, and other creative professionals.
The firm maintains offices in New York City and Los Angeles.
The acquisition expands Focus’s portfolio of specialized business management firms and provides MLM with access to additional resources and infrastructure.
Focus reported more than $550 billion in collectively advised assets as of June 30, 2026.
Expanding Focus’s Entertainment Industry Capabilities
The acquisition strengthens Focus Financial Partners’ presence in a specialized segment of the financial services industry.
Business management firms serving entertainment professionals often provide services tailored to clients with complex financial affairs and careers involving multiple income sources.
These clients may include performers, producers, directors, writers, and executives working across television, film, and other entertainment businesses.
ML Management Partners has developed its business around these relationships over nearly four decades.
The firm’s experience extends beyond traditional entertainment industry clients to include family office services for high-net-worth individuals.
Focus believes the acquisition supports its broader strategy of building a platform that combines specialized financial expertise with extensive operational resources.
The company has continued investing in businesses that complement its wealth management and family office services.
MLM adds an established client base and experienced leadership team to that platform.
ML Management Partners’ Nearly Four-Decade History
ML Management Partners was founded in 1988 by Mark Landesman.
The business initially focused primarily on serving comedians before expanding its services across the broader entertainment industry.
Today, MLM works with professionals both in front of and behind the camera, including talent, executives, producers, directors, and writers.
Its client base also includes individuals and businesses with specialized financial management requirements.
The firm operates from New York City with a second office in Los Angeles, providing a presence in two important centers of the U.S. entertainment industry.
Landesman has emphasized the importance of maintaining long-term relationships and personalized services for the firm’s clients.
He described the acquisition as an opportunity to preserve MLM’s established approach while accessing the broader resources of Focus.

articles.text:
SA’s Yoco secures $100m credit facility to scale merchant cash advances
0
By
Tom Jackson
on
November 16, 2026
News , Southern Africa
South African fintech company Yoco has secured a US$100 million credit facility from US investment firm Victory Park Capital to expand its merchant cash advance operation.
Yoco builds tools and services to help small businesses accept card payments in-store and online, access loans, and manage their day to day activities. The startup has advanced more than ZAR6.5 billion (US$395 million) to over 40,000 merchants since 2018, working with specialist credit providers.
The company, which secured US$83 million in Series C funding back in 2021, has now secured a US$100 million credit facility from Victory Park Capital, which will allow it to scale its cash advance operations, and gain greater control over the pricing and risk of its merchant loans.
The aim is to use the transaction data generated by merchants using Yoco’s card machines and online payment tools to assess businesses that traditional lenders may struggle to evaluate, helping the company turn its payments relationship with more than 200,000 businesses into a larger cash advance operation.
“We have spent a decade building an operating system that runs a merchant’s whole business, payments, point of sale, and now the decisions in between. Financing was the one layer we didn’t fully control. This facility changes that,” said Yoco CEO Carsten Holtkemeyer.
Victory Park Capital brings experience in private credit and asset-backed finance to the arrangement, having invested more than US$12 billion across 260 investments since 2007. Senior partner Jason Brown, said Yoco had demonstrated a track record of supporting small and independent businesses.
“We’re supportive of Yoco’s mission to expand access to flexible financing solutions for South African entrepreneurs,” he said.

articles.text:
Seawolf Therapeutics: $100 Million Funding And Up To $1.2 Billion Sanofi Partnership To Advance DNA Medicines
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:32 AM
Seawolf Therapeutics: $100 Million Funding And Up To $1.2 Billion Sanofi Partnership To Advance DNA Medicines
Seawolf Therapeutics, a San Diego-based biotechnology company developing DNA-based medicines, has emerged from stealth with $100 million in funding and announced a multi-target research collaboration with Sanofi worth up to $1.2 billion in potential milestone payments, plus royalties. The company is developing a lipid nanoparticle-based DNA delivery platform designed to enable sustained production of therapeutic proteins inside patients’ cells.
Seawolf’s financing includes seed and Series A investments backed by Versant Ventures, MPM BioImpact, Novartis Venture Fund, Eli Lilly, CRISPR Therapeutics, Sixty Degree Capital, Alexandria Venture Investments, and Pathway to Cures, the philanthropic venture arm of the National Bleeding Disorders Foundation.
Versant Ventures led the seed financing, while the Series A included Versant, MPM BioImpact, and Novartis Venture Fund.
The capital will support advancement of Seawolf’s proprietary therapeutic pipeline, including a lead program targeting metabolic diseases.
Developing The TRIDENT DNA Delivery Platform
Seawolf’s technology platform, called TRIDENT, stands for Targeted RNA-Induced DNA Expression via Nuclear Translocation.
The system uses lipid nanoparticles to transport DNA into cells and facilitate access to the nucleus, where genetic information can support production of therapeutic proteins.
Lipid nanoparticles are also used in certain RNA-based medicines, but RNA therapies can face limitations involving how long protein expression lasts.
Seawolf is developing a different approach intended to provide more durable protein production by delivering DNA-based payloads.
TRIDENT combines a proprietary lipid nanoparticle, DNA encoding a therapeutic protein, and an auxiliary factor that helps facilitate nuclear entry.
The company says its technology has demonstrated sustained protein expression above therapeutic levels in nonhuman primate studies at doses reported to be safe and well tolerated.
The company has also generated preclinical proof-of-concept results in animal models involving metabolic and rare diseases.
These findings remain preclinical and will require further evaluation before therapeutic benefits and safety can be established in humans.
A Redosable Approach To DNA Medicines
Seawolf is designing its technology to allow repeat administration when necessary.
The company describes TRIDENT as a nonviral DNA delivery approach that avoids some of the limitations associated with virus-based genetic medicine platforms.
Its goal is to provide durable protein expression while preserving the ability to adjust or supplement dosing.
The technology could support several therapeutic approaches, including replacement of defective genes and systemic production of biologic medicines.
Seawolf believes this flexibility may allow the platform to address multiple disease categories.
Sanofi Collaboration Includes Up To $1.2 Billion In Milestones
Alongside its funding announcement, Seawolf disclosed a multi-target research collaboration and exclusive license agreement with Sanofi.
The partnership will focus on developing undisclosed therapies for bleeding disorders and additional indications.

Trinity Capital Inc. Provides $100 Million in Debt Financing to Accelerate Phononic's Growth and Manufacturing Expansion for AI Data Centers
News provided by
Trinity Capital Inc.
Nov 17, 2026, 08:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
PHOENIX , Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Trinity Capital Inc. (NYSE: TRIN ), a leading alternative asset manager, today announced the commitment of $100 million in debt financing to Phononic, a North Carolina-based company developing solid-state cooling solutions for AI data centers. The financing will support accelerated growth and manufacturing capacity expansion to meet increasing customer demand.
Phononic's proprietary Thermal Control Systems™ provide software-defined cooling for AI infrastructure by combining high-performance thermoelectric devices with intelligent controls. Compact, solid-state devices and an integrated software control layer deliver precision cooling at the point of need for critical components, including GPUs, high-bandwidth memory, networking silicon, and the optical transceivers that connect them. Phononic's Thermal Fabric™ software layer monitors conditions throughout the data center and dynamically adjusts thermal control in real time as AI workloads change. Together, these solutions are designed to unlock greater AI infrastructure performance, optimize compute and facility capacity, and reduce energy and water consumption.
"As AI hardware continues to evolve, we believe precise, real-time cooling at the chip level is becoming increasingly important," said Phil Gager, Senior Managing Director of Tech Lending at Trinity Capital. "Phononic has built the thermoelectric technology and software to address that need, and we're pleased to back their team as demand for their solutions continues to build."
Phononic enters its next phase of growth as a profitable company backed by leading venture and growth-equity investors. With demand accelerating across AI infrastructure, the company is expanding manufacturing capacity to meet growing customer requirements and scale delivery of its intelligent thermal control solutions.
"AI infrastructure is advancing at an unprecedented pace, and cooling has become a critical bottleneck to growth, limiting both facility capacity and compute and optical performance. Our customers are demanding disruptive thermal control solutions that can overcome these limitations at scale," said Dr. Tony Atti, CEO and Founder of Phononic. "Our partnership with Trinity Capital enables us to accelerate manufacturing capacity expansion to meet that demand and support the next wave of growth across AI infrastructure."
About Trinity Capital Inc.
Trinity Capital Inc. (NYSE: TRIN ) is an alternative asset manager that seeks to deliver consistent returns for investors through access to private credit markets. Trinity Capital sources and structures investments in well-capitalized growth-oriented companies across five distinct lending verticals: Tech Lending, Equipment Finance, Healthcare & Life Sciences, Sponsor Finance, and Asset Based Lending. As a long-term, trusted partner for innovative companies seeking tailored debt solutions, Trinity Capital has deployed more than $6.8 billion across over 511 investments since inception in 2008 (as of September 30, 2026). Headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona, Trinity Capital's dedicated team is strategically located across the United States and Europe. articles.title: Adaspace Hong Kong IPO Raises $95.6 Million for AI Satellites
articles.snippet: Adaspace Hong Kong IPO Raises $95.6 Million for AI Satellites iNews Zoombangla
articles.text:
Adaspace Technology raised HK$750 million ($95.6 million) in a Hong Kong initial public offering, and its shares moved higher by the midday break after opening below the offer price. The debut puts a listed supplier of AI-powered satellites and satellite-data services on the market as the company seeks funding for research, production and facilities.
Reuters reported that the shares opened at HK$24.44, 1.8% below the HK$24.90 offer price, and were last at HK$24.60 in its morning report. Bamboo Works later reported a rise to HK$25.26 by the midday break, 1.45% above the offer price. Those are snapshots from different points in Friday’s session; neither is a closing price.
The Chengdu-based company sold 30.12 million shares at HK$24.90 each, the bottom of its marketed range of HK$24.90 to HK$33.20, Reuters reported. The wire also said the retail tranche was subscribed 3.43 times and the international offering was covered 1.79 times. Those figures describe separate parts of the offering and should not be combined as one subscription measure.
Reuters describes Adaspace as a maker of AI-powered satellites that also provides satellite-data services. The Hong Kong exchange’s November 12 global-offering announcement identifies Adaspace Technology and refers investors to the company’s November 5 prospectus. The filing is the primary record for the offering; Reuters and Bamboo Works provide independent reports on the first trading session.
Bamboo Works reported net proceeds of HK$652 million ($83.6 million). It said the company plans to use 35.6% of that amount to strengthen research and development, 24.4% to build a center in Shenzhen, 20% for strategic investments and acquisitions, and 10% to repay bank loans. These are the allocations listed in the report; they do not account for every part of the proceeds.
The same report gave a snapshot of the company’s recent finances. Adaspace recorded first-half 2026 revenue of 226 million yuan ($33.9 million), down 6.3% from a year earlier. Its net loss narrowed 21.5% to 150 million yuan. The revenue decline and narrower loss are separate measures, so the loss reduction does not mean revenue grew.
For the Adaspace Hong Kong IPO, the distinction between the amount raised and the net proceeds matters: Reuters reported the HK$750 million raise, while Bamboo Works cited HK$652 million in net proceeds. The reports also show a share price that first fell below the offer price and later moved above it by midday, without establishing the final close.
The debut marks the start of public trading for the company’s shares, while the planned research, production and Shenzhen spending remain future uses of the funds. The available reports do not establish how quickly those investments will translate into additional satellites, data services or revenue. They document the offering terms, early trading and the company’s stated financial results, leaving later operating performance to subsequent disclosures.

articles.title: LibertyStream Advances Up To $95 Million Financing And Signs New Lithium Sales Agreement
articles.snippet:
LibertyStream Infrastructure Partners has extended its financing exclusivity period with Endurance Finance Partners through January 15, 2027 as the companies continue working toward a proposed financing package of up to $95 million.
The post LibertyStream Advances Up To $95 Million Financing And Signs New Lithium Sales Agreement appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
LibertyStream Advances Up To $95 Million Financing And Signs New Lithium Sales Agreement
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 9:32 AM
LibertyStream Advances Up To $95 Million Financing And Signs New Lithium Sales Agreement
LibertyStream Infrastructure Partners has extended its financing exclusivity period with Endurance Finance Partners through January 15, 2027 as the companies continue working toward a proposed financing package of up to $95 million.
Endurance is acting as arranger for the financing framework, which is intended to support LibertyStream’s Freedom 1, Freedom 2 and potentially additional lithium production sites.
The original non-binding financing term sheet was announced on September 3, 2026.
All other terms remain unchanged.
LibertyStream said the additional exclusivity period will allow definitive financing documentation to be coordinated with its broader capital plan.
The proposed financing remains subject to due diligence, investment and credit approvals, definitive agreements, required corporate and regulatory approvals and other customary conditions.
Future project sites would require separate approvals.
The company also disclosed a new commercial agreement supporting its planned lithium production.
On November 4, 2026, LibertyStream entered into a sales contract with a major international cathode manufacturer supplying the U.S. market.
The agreement covers 500 tonnes of lithium carbonate in 2027 and up to an additional 17,000 tonnes between 2028 and 2031.
The 2028 through 2031 volumes remain subject to execution of a long-term supply agreement.
LibertyStream previously entered into a separate offtake agreement in July 2026 with a U.S. industrial customer for 600 tonnes of lithium carbonate annually over five years.
The company is developing technology designed to produce lithium carbonate from oilfield brine.
Its strategy involves deploying proprietary direct lithium extraction technology into existing oil and gas infrastructure, an approach intended to lower capital costs and reduce project development risk.
LibertyStream is working to develop Freedom 1 and Freedom 2 as it seeks to become an early commercial-scale North American producer of lithium carbonate from oilfield brines.
The proposed Endurance financing could provide capital to advance those projects, although LibertyStream said there is no assurance that definitive financing agreements or its proposed Nasdaq listing will be completed.
